subject: Post-call: VPC dataflow & egress walkthrough + owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@medallion-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: VPC dataflow & egress walkthrough + owners

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before the technical follow-up: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Medallion requires a private deployment (VPC) with no outbound internet by default for inference nodes.
- PII classification: patient identifiers (name, MRN, DOB) must never be persisted in plaintext outside customer-controlled storage.
- Retention: logs and model audit trails retained for 7 years for specific clinical investigations; shorter retention (180 days) acceptable for operational logs.
- Audit/logging: application telemetry must be forwarded to your Splunk cluster (customer-managed) or exported as syslog; access to raw request payloads must be tightly controlled.
- Data residency: production inference must run in Medallion's us-east-1 VPC; backups or non-prod may be in us-west-2 if encrypted with customer-managed KMS.
- Air-gap option: CISO asked about an on-prem air-gapped install for an isolated environment for high-risk PII processing.

Attachments: I uploaded a one-page MOP and the sketch you shared — medallion_initial_boundary_sketch.pdf and redwood_postcall_mop.pdf.

Proposed owners & immediate next steps (please confirm):
1) Tech deep-dive with infra architect to map exact subnets, NAT/no-NAT constraints, and any required egress allowlist (owner: Ben Carter).
2) Security runbook review: KMS/HSM keycontrol and audit trail gating (owner: Neha Kapoor).
3) Deliverable: a constrained dataflow diagram showing exactly where PII is transformed/retained and a recommended retention config for logs & traces (owner: Soojin Lee).

Can we schedule the infra deep-dive for this Thursday or Friday (30-60 minute session)? Please tell us who from Medallion will attend (CISO or infra lead preferred).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

From: Alex Hunter <alex.hunter@medallion-health.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC dataflow & egress walkthrough + owners

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Carmen (CISO) and I reviewed; a few clarifications from our side before the infra call: 

1) Air-gapped requirement: for our highest-risk workflows we cannot allow any egress (no DNS, no outbound TLS). We still want Redwood to run inference but must evaluate a fully offline on-prem option. Is Redwood's private package compatible with our air-gap compliance program?

2) KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys are mandatory for any storage of model checkpoints or logs containing patient identifiers. We need an option where your runtime never has access to the plaintext keys (HSM-backed decryption inside our VPC).

3) Telemetry: we will prefer push to our Splunk endpoint (syslog over TLS). If Redwood needs to capture traces for debugging, it must be sampled, redacted (no raw PII), and stored only in a customer-controlled S3 bucket encrypted with our KMS.

4) Retention: 7 years for audit traces is a hard requirement for certain datasets. Operational logs can be trimmed at 180 days. Please confirm Redwood can support configurable retention at the route/model level.

I've attached the network boundary sketch (medallion_initial_boundary_sketch.pdf) with some internal notes. Carmen is available for the infra deep-dive Friday 10:00–11:00 PT.

Alex
IT Security / Medallion Health
alex.hunter@medallion-health.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-call: VPC dataflow & egress walkthrough + owners

Team — summary of quick feasibility notes and our proposed approach for the Friday deep-dive with Medallion: 

Feasibility highlights: 
- Private/VPC deployment: supported. We'll provision inference nodes into a customer VPC (BYO VPC peering or PrivateLink) so compute never traverses public internet.
- No-Egress (air-gap) path: we have two realistic options:
  A) Fully air-gapped on-prem package — offline installer + pre-signed model bundles delivered via secure courier or SFTP to a jump box inside customer network. This satisfies "no outbound internet" but increases release cadence friction and means debugging traces are local.
  B) VPC-only with egress-blocked subnets + allowlist for outbound telemetry to customer's Splunk or audit endpoints (if they accept).
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS; for HSM-backed keys we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or an on-prem HSM using a KMIP bridge. Important: ensure key material never leaves customer control.
- Logs & retention: runtime can be configured to redact request bodies at the token level; audit traces can be exported to customer S3 with lifecycle policy (we can parameterize 180 days / 7 years per data class).

Risks / open questions to confirm with Medallion Friday:
1) Will they accept outbound TLS to a small allowlist (Splunk IPs) for telemetry, or is zero egress mandatory across the board?
2) If air-gap option chosen, who will approve the courier or transfer mechanism for model bundles?
3) Which dataset(s) require 7-year retention — we need to map retention class to routes so we can implement the life-cycle policy correctly.

Suggested Friday agenda (30–45 min):
- 5m: Introductions & scope confirmation (Sojourn).
- 15m: Walk the medallion_initial_boundary_sketch.pdf; map subnets, NAT, and endpoints (Ben).
- 10m: Security controls — KMS/HSM options and logging/export mechanics (Neha).
- 10m: Deliverables & timeline (Sojourn / Marissa).

Deliverables we will bring next week: updated dataflow diagram (redwood internal), a short decision matrix comparing air-gap vs VPC-allowlist, and a draft retention configuration per route. I'll attach the proposed_action_items.md to the Drive before the call.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
